classification.difficultyReason: Represent the repeated roots, choose two symmetric relations for elimination, factor the resulting quadratic, and reject a candidate using the unused product relation.

content.prompt: Find the roots of $x^3-x^2-16x-20=0$ given that 2 of the roots are equal.

answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha,\alpha,\beta$.

Sum of roots:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\alpha+\beta&=1\\\beta&=1-2\alpha\qquad(1)\end{aligned}$$
Sum of products taken two at a time:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\alpha\beta+\alpha\beta&=-16\qquad(2)\end{aligned}$$
Product of roots:
$$\alpha^2\beta=20\qquad(3)$$
Substituting (1) into (2):
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+2\alpha(1-2\alpha)&=-16\\-3\alpha^2+2\alpha&=-16\\3\alpha^2-2\alpha-16&=0\end{aligned}$$
PSF (Product, Sum, Factors): Product $=3\times(-16)=-48$, Sum $=-2$, Factors: $-8$ and $6$.
$$\begin{aligned}3\alpha^2-8\alpha+6\alpha-16&=0\\\alpha(3\alpha-8)+2(3\alpha-8)&=0\\(3\alpha-8)(\alpha+2)&=0\\\alpha&=\frac83\text{ or }-2\end{aligned}$$
If $\alpha=\dfrac83$, then $\beta=1-\dfrac{16}{3}=-\dfrac{13}{3}$ and $\alpha^2\beta=\dfrac{64}{9}\left(-\dfrac{13}{3}\right)\ne20$, so (3) fails.

If $\alpha=-2$, then $\beta=1-2(-2)=5$ and $\alpha^2\beta=4(5)=20$, so (3) holds.

The roots are $x=-2,-2,5$.
